title: How to start a compost pile that doesn't stink

lines.show: You want free {g:fertilizer} for your garden.
So you dump your kitchen {y:scraps} in a pile.
Two weeks later, it {r:stinks}.
Too many wet {r:greens}, not enough air.
So you add {y:browns}:
dry leaves, cardboard, straw.
About {y:two parts} brown to one part green.
Then {r:rats} show up.
So no {y:meat}, no dairy, no oil.
The middle gets {r:soggy} and sour.
So you {y:turn} it every week.
In summer, it dries out and {r:stops}.
So you keep it damp, like a wrung-out {y:sponge}.
And you build it on bare {y:soil},
so {g:worms} can move in.
A few months later, it's dark and {g:crumbly}
and smells like a forest floor.
{y:Congratulations}.
You built a compost pile
that feeds your garden for {g:free}.
